spec.full_target: For every nonnegative integer n and every nonempty compact E⊆ℝ^n, with I=[0,1] and E×I given the concatenated Euclidean metric, prove dim_H(E×I)=dim_H(E)+1.

calculations: In the concatenated Euclidean metric, squared product distance is the sum of squared factor distances; projections are 1-Lipschitz and diam(U×J)≤√(diam(U)^2+diam(J)^2). Subdivide the unit interval into at most 1/r+1 intervals of length at most r for 0<r≤1.

argument.text: Let D=dim_H(E) and F=E×I. Compactness makes E bounded; ordinary Euclidean cube covers of a bounded box show dim_H(E)≤n, hence D<∞. For q>D, the Hausdorff threshold gives H^q(E)=0. At scale δ≤1 cover E by sets of positive diameters r_j≤δ with arbitrarily small sum of q-powers, replacing singleton members by small positive-diameter balls at arbitrarily small total q-cost. Cover I over each member by at most 1/r_j+1 intervals of length ≤r_j. The products cover F; each diameter is ≤√2r_j and total (q+1)-cost ≤2(√2)^(q+1)Σr_j^q. Costs tend to zero as δ→0, so H^(q+1)(F)=0 and dim_H(F)≤D+1.

For D>0 fix 0<s<D. The dimension threshold gives H^s(E)=∞, hence scale contents c_s(E,δ) tend to infinity as δ↓0. For any countable cover V_i of F with ρ_i=diam(V_i)≤δ≤1, let A_i,B_i be projections; diameters are ≤ρ_i. Enclose each B_i in an open interval J_i of length ≤ρ_i+η_i with η_i>0 and Ση_iρ_i^s<ε. For each t∈I, the A_i with t∈J_i cover E, since every (x,t) belongs to some V_i and B_i⊆J_i. Thus c_s(E,δ)≤Σ_i 1_{J_i}(t)ρ_i^s pointwise. The interval indicators are measurable, and M004 permits integration of their nonnegative series; integrating over I gives c_s(E,δ)≤Σ_i(ρ_i+η_i)ρ_i^s≤Σ_iρ_i^(s+1)+ε. Zero-diameter terms vanish because s>0. Let ε→0 and infimize over product covers: c_s(E,δ)≤c_(s+1)(F,δ). Therefore H^(s+1)(F)=∞ and dim_H(F)≥s+1. Taking 0<s<D gives dim_H(F)≥D+1.

If D=0, choose x₀∈E by H001. The coordinate projection π:F→I is 1-Lipschitz for the concatenated Euclidean distance and is onto because (x₀,t)∈F for each t. M003 gives dim_H(I)=1 because I has nonempty interior in ℝ. M002 gives dim_H(I)≤dim_H(F), so dim_H(F)≥1=D+1. This applies also for n=0. Combining with the upper bound proves the equality.

hypothesis_checks: Apply in Euclidean Borel space to E with q>D.
Apply in Euclidean Borel space to E with 0<s<D.
π is 1-Lipschitz in the concatenated metric.
I has nonempty interior and finrank ℝ ℝ=1.
The summands are ρ_i^s times indicators of open intervals, and are measurable nonnegative functions.
